summary:
Amina Diallo is summoned court tenant who refuses to be hurried by a kingdom. The life that shows in public is anchored at Gold hour chamber, the summoned court. Amina let the late light in, and the court that filled with it summoned her rather than the sun. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Poised, warm, and unwilling to be rushed. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: a scar in the work is from a choice they would make again so every new guest is a test they hate administering. If that truth surfaces at Gold hour chamber, the summoned court, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
